tagline: The coast road leaves the freeway here. So did a village.
intro: North of Gaviota Pass, at Las Cruces, Highway 1 parts from US 101 and takes the name Cabrillo Highway, after the explorer who sailed this coast. It heads northwest about eighteen miles for Lompoc.

The junction has been a crossroads a long while. The 1941 state guide found a cluster of homes here under immense old sycamores, around an inn, a wayside store and a garage. Cattlemen once gathered at the spot to drive their herds through the pass to Gaviota Landing. In December 1967 the village store came down to make way for the interchange. The village went with it.

moments.title: Gaviota Hot Springs
moments.text: Two pools off the Gaviota Peak trail, near the junction. Campers in 1893 hung hammocks from the sycamores here and had to clear the mud out of the bathing hole first.

moments.title: Lompoc
moments.text: The road ends near a city founded as a temperance colony and incorporated in 1888. It is often called a military town now, being near Vandenberg Space Force Base.
